comparator.name: Medicine
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 EER applies to the September 2026 DNUA entry cohort. Appendix 1b controls the 165 EC of compulsory Medicine and Article 3.6 the 15 EC of approved second-year electives. Bewegen & Waarnemen and Levensloop are each 10 EC under the adopted regulations. Three compulsory 3 EC carousel courses are taken in Year 1 and the remaining one in Year 2. The 1 EC longitudinal progress test is counted once. Article 4.2b specifies entry to the preparation block, workplace course and thesis, and Articles 5.5 and 5.6 specify progress and workplace assessment.

alternatives.labelRationale: Seventeen health, psychology, cognition and biomedical courses form the core, supported by sociology, qualitative inquiry, statistics, data analysis, ethical reasoning and persuasive communication plus PPD. alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Six courses / 45 EC differ in each direction. Molecular cell biology, biochemistry, molecular pathology, infection/immunity, mechanisms of disease and laboratory work give way to perception/action, language neuroscience, social psychology, sociology, qualitative inquiry and persuasive communication. The organising priority changes from molecular/organ-system disease investigation to cognitive, psychological and social connections between physical and mental health.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete programmes are included in sequence. Prevention and disease management (14925) are already substantively represented through epidemiology, disease mechanisms, immunity, pharmacology and health psychology in the closest response and through health behaviour and psychological intervention in the second. Scientific and ethical practice (14926) is implemented through research methods, evidence synthesis and ethical reasoning. No remaining generator-eligible row supplies a further distinct academic priority: clinical diagnosis/treatment and symptoms (14920/14923) remain explicit gaps, not a licence to substitute a computing or generic leadership programme. A third reorganisation of these same evidenced concerns is not included merely by swapping courses. Public health, imaging and doctor-patient communication are support-only curricular topics; alone they do not generate additional routes.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both address biological foundations of health and disease. UCR focuses on cells, metabolism and genetics.
UCR Human Physiology studies circulation and breathing. Utrecht connects those systems to symptoms and clinical reasoning.
UCR Biochemistry studies metabolism at the molecular level. Utrecht also integrates digestive-system medicine.
UCR Pharmacology studies drug action, kinetics and adverse effects. Utrecht places drug treatment within the medical curriculum.
